scope.summary: tools/run_nahw_evals.py replays each row through tools/fusha_nahw_particle_rules, which decides PARTICLE IDENTITY from the content-letter diacritic (rule + branch). That comparison is real, and so is the evidence-ablation mutation. It does NOT decide the typed grammatical STATE: several distinct states share one A/B branch, so mapping a branch onto a state would assert a state the consumer never computed. The state axes are therefore compared against a COMMITTED per-case binding (which catches a mutated axis) and reported state_comparison=fixture_only. The same gap quarantines ten hover rows: nine have no consumer at all (referent, polysemy, proper-noun, imperative), and in_conditional_referent_free_safe cannot be decided because an_vs_inna branch B covers both light conditional and heavy emphatic. This packet builds the typed consumer.
